transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well, hello Doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me. Um... I suppose what brings me in is, well, my wife. She seems to think I'm not eating quite enough lately. But honestly, most days I just have a little coffee and some toast in the morning, and then... maybe just some light soup or a few vegetables later on. 

I mean, at my age, big heavy meals just feel so unnecessary, you know? You don't really need all that food when you're not out working anymore. Does that make sense? I hope it's alright that I'm taking up your time with this, I just wanted to do the right thing and put her mind at ease.
Have you noticed any significant weight loss recently, or has your weight stayed about the same despite eating less?

Well, um... I suppose I have lost a little bit. My regular doctor did mention recently that the number on the scale has gotten a bit too low for his liking. But, honestly, I don't see it as a bad thing at all. 

To me, being a little lighter just makes it so much easier to get around the garden, you know? And it really helps me keep up on my daily walks without feeling so weighed down or tired out. That's a good thing for someone my age, isn't it? I certainly don't want to cause a fuss or make anyone worry, I just figure it's healthier to be on the lighter side.
Have you noticed a decreased interest in eating or a lack of appetite lately?

Well, um... I wouldn't say I've lost interest, exactly. I still enjoy a nice cup of coffee, and I like the taste of the soup my wife makes. It's just... I suppose I just don't feel that strong urge to eat big meals anymore. 

It's not that I don't have an appetite at all, it's just that a little bit seems to satisfy me perfectly fine these days. I mean, as you get older, your stomach just doesn't need as much, right? I'm sure you hear that from a lot of folks my age. It's perfectly normal to not want a heavy plate of food, isn't it? I just try to listen to my body, and right now, it's just telling me it doesn't need much. That's a reasonable way to look at it, don't you think?
Have you had any trouble chewing, swallowing, or keeping food down lately?

Oh, no, no trouble like that at all. Goodness, no. My teeth are holding up alright for an old fellow, and swallowing is just fine. And I certainly don't have any trouble keeping things down once I've eaten them. 

Everything works just the way it's supposed to, thankfully. It's really just that I don't need to put as much *into* the system, if that makes sense. I wouldn't want you to think there was anything physically wrong with my stomach or my throat. I'm actually in pretty good shape for my age, wouldn't you say? I mean, as far as all that plumbing goes, anyway.
Have you been feeling more tired than usual or lacking in energy lately, even if you're getting enough rest?

Well, um... no, I wouldn't say that. I mean, sure, I'm not a spring chicken anymore, so maybe I enjoy a quiet sit-down in the afternoon, but... I don't feel unusually tired, no. 

Actually, I feel like I have quite a bit of energy for my age. Like I was saying before, I still get out for my daily walks and putter around the garden just fine. I really think staying a bit lighter on my feet actually helps keep my energy up, you know? It just takes less effort to move around. I sleep quite well at night, too. I think I'm doing pretty well in the energy department, wouldn't you agree? I certainly wouldn't want you to worry that I'm just wasting away or sitting around the house all day, because I'm really quite active!
Doctor: Have you found yourself forgetting to eat, or not even thinking about food as much as you used to?

Oh, goodness, no. I don't think I ever just... forget. My wife is wonderful about keeping us on a nice, regular schedule, you know? We always sit down together for our meals. I definitely still think about food, and I always appreciate what she puts on the table. 

It's really just... well, like I mentioned, I just take much smaller portions when we do sit down. I'm very responsible about making sure I have my meals, I promise you that. It's important to keep a good routine, isn't it? I wouldn't want you to think I'm neglecting myself or getting forgetful in my old age. I always make sure to sit down and have my little bits of food throughout the day. That's a good, sensible habit to keep, right?
Can you tell me how much weight you've lost recently, and whether this was intentional or not?

Well, I suppose I have lost a little bit of weight. My regular doctor did mention that the number on the scale has gotten a bit too low for his liking. But, honestly, I didn't set out to lose a whole lot of weight on purpose, it just sort of happened as I started eating those smaller portions. 

And, really, I don't see it as a bad thing. Being a bit lighter... it actually makes it so much easier for me to get around the garden and keep up on my daily walks. My knees don't ache as much, you know? It just feels better to not carry around extra bulk at my age. I'm just trying to stay active and healthy, and being lighter helps with that, don't you think? I'm certainly not trying to cause any worry, I just want to stay on my feet as long as I can.
Have you been feeling down, sad, or losing interest in things you used to enjoy lately?

Oh, no, not at all. I mean... I think I'm generally a pretty cheerful fellow. I certainly haven't been feeling down or sad, no. 

And I definitely haven't lost interest in the things I love. Like I was saying, I still get out into the garden every single day, and my wife and I always watch our evening programs together. I really do enjoy my days, I promise you. I think keeping busy and trying to maintain a positive outlook is the best way to go about things at my age, don't you agree? I wouldn't want you to worry that I'm just sitting around feeling sorry for myself or getting depressed, because I'm really quite content. I'm doing just fine in that regard, I really am.
Do you find that you're eating less because you don't feel hungry, or do you start feeling full much sooner than before?

Well, I suppose... it's just that I don't need as much as I used to. I don't think I feel full any sooner, really, and I wouldn't say I've lost my appetite. It's more that... well, at my age, you just don't burn as much energy, do you? 

I just try to be sensible about it. I don't want to overeat or make myself uncomfortable, so I just take those smaller portions. It's really just about listening to my body and giving it what it needs, and nothing more. That's the right way to do it, isn't it? I just want to make sure I'm not overdoing it. I feel perfectly fine, I assure you.
Do you feel like you get full very quickly, even when you haven't eaten much?

Well, no, not really. I don't think it's that I get full too quickly... it's just that I don't dish out very much to begin with. 

I mean, if I sat down to a big plate like I used to when I was working, I'm sure I'd eat it, but... I just don't need all that food anymore. So, no, I wouldn't say I get full after just a few bites or anything strange like that. I just eat what I've decided is a sensible amount for a man my age, and then I'm done. That makes sense, doesn't it? I'm just trying to be careful not to overindulge.
Have you noticed that even when you eat your usual amounts, you still seem to be losing weight without trying?

Oh, no, I wouldn't say that. I haven't noticed anything like that at all. I mean, my weight has always been pretty steady, you know? 

I suppose I might have lost a pound or two here and there, but that's just because I'm eating those sensible portions we talked about. It's certainly not happening on its own, and I'm definitely not wasting away or anything concerning like that. I think my weight is just fine for a man my age. I'm taking good care of myself, I really am. I hope you don't think I'm neglecting my health, because I'm trying my best to stay in good shape. That's the important thing, right?
Have you noticed any weight loss even when you've been eating the same amount as usual?

Well, I... I think we just covered that, didn't we? But no, I haven't seen anything like that. If I'm eating my usual amount, my weight stays right where it should be. 

It's only when I'm being careful with my portions that I might drop a tiny bit, but that's perfectly normal, isn't it? I mean, anyone would lose a little if they cut back just a touch. I'm certainly not losing weight for no reason at all. I keep a close eye on these things, you know. I wouldn't let myself get unhealthy, I promise you that. I'm doing all right, aren't I?
Have you ever noticed yourself losing weight even when you haven't changed how much you eat?

I... I'm sorry, doctor, I feel like I must be frustrating you. You've asked me that a few times now, and I—I really don't mean to be difficult or give you the wrong answer. 

But honestly, no, it just doesn't happen like that for me. If I eat my regular meals, my weight stays exactly the same. It never just drops off on its own. I only ever lose anything if I've been... well, extra careful about what I'm taking in for a few days. 

I hope I'm not misunderstanding what you're getting at? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the information you need. I'm really trying to be helpful here.
Have you ever noticed yourself losing weight even when you haven't changed how much you eat?

I'm so sorry, doctor. I know we just went over this, and I really don't want to waste your time by making you repeat yourself. I must not be explaining myself very well. 

But to answer your question again... no, I haven't noticed anything like that. My weight has never just slipped away on its own. If I eat my usual meals, I stay exactly the same. It's only when I'm being very disciplined about my portions that the scale moves down at all, and even then, it's just a sensible amount. 

I really hope I'm answering this the way you need me to. I'm doing my best to be clear, I promise. Is there... is there something specific you're looking for me to say? I want to make sure I'm doing this right.
Even if you've been eating the same amount, have you ever noticed your clothes feeling looser or your weight going down without trying?

Oh, goodness... I'm so sorry, doctor. I know you're just trying to be thorough, and I feel terrible that I must not be giving you the right answer since you have to keep asking. I really am trying to be helpful.

But... no, I haven't noticed my clothes feeling looser or anything like that unless I've been intentionally cutting back. If I eat my normal amount, my trousers fit exactly the same as they always do. My weight doesn't just drop on its own without me trying. I promise I'm keeping a close eye on everything, and I wouldn't let things get out of hand. 

I hope that's what you were asking? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information. I'm doing okay, aren't I?
Even when you’ve been eating the same amount as usual, have you ever noticed yourself losing weight without trying?

I... oh dear, I'm so sorry. I feel like I'm failing a test here, and I really don't mean to be difficult. I know you've asked this a few different ways now, and I just... I must be missing something you're looking for. 

But, honestly, no. It just never happens that way for me. If I eat my usual meals, nothing changes. The scale doesn't move, my clothes don't get baggy... I don't lose anything unless I'm actively, you know, being very strict with myself. 

I'm so sorry if I'm frustrating you. I'm really trying my best to give you the right answer. Am I... am I doing this okay? I just want to make sure I'm being a good patient for you.
Even when you’ve been eating your usual amount of food, have you ever noticed yourself losing weight without trying?

Oh, my... I really am making a mess of this, aren't I? I am so, so sorry to make you ask me this yet again. I feel like such a nuisance, and I promise I'm not trying to be difficult or hide anything from you. 

It's just that, well... no. I've never lost weight without trying. At my age, the scale really doesn't budge unless I'm being extremely careful with what I put on my plate. If I just ate my usual meals without thinking about it, I'd stay the exact same weight. It never just drops off on its own. 

I'm so sorry, I know that's the exact same thing I said before. Am I... did I misunderstand the question, maybe? Please tell me if I need to explain it differently. I really just want to be helpful to you.
